slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Not covered here? Ask us directly — same working day response.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Yes, properly rather than reluctantly. That means day-to-day support for macOS, central device management, endpoint security, and the Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace side of things on Mac. We’ll respond the same working day, and where something needs hands on the hardware one of our field engineers attends.

slots.label: Question 2
slots.default: Can you support a mix of Mac and Windows?

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Yes, and it is the more common situation. The important part is joining the two together rather than running them as separate worlds: one directory and one sign-in for everybody, shared files in SharePoint and OneDrive instead of a legacy file share, and the same security rules applied on both platforms. Handled that way, people stop noticing which one they are on.

slots.label: Question 3
slots.default: Do you manage Macs with MDM?

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: Yes. Mobile device management is what makes a Mac fleet manageable at all. With Apple Business Manager and automated enrolment, devices configure themselves on first boot, settings such as encryption and screen lock are applied centrally, apps and updates are pushed on a schedule, and a lost device can be locked or wiped remotely.

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: In a business context, yes. macOS has strong built-in protections in Gatekeeper, XProtect and System Integrity Protection, but those are silent and local: they will not tell you that a device is unpatched, that encryption was turned off, or that something was run anyway. Managed endpoint protection adds the central visibility and alerting that distinguishes a protected fleet from a set of individually hopeful laptops.

slots.label: Paragraph 6
slots.default: Yes. The five controls are platform-neutral, and a Mac fleet meets them the same way a Windows one does: the firewall enabled, secure configuration applied and held, administrator rights controlled, malware protection in place, and operating system plus application updates installed within the required window. We are Cyber Essentials Certified ourselves and include Macs in scope rather than carving them out.

slots.label: Question 6
slots.default: Can you set up a Mac for a new starter without it coming to us first?

slots.label: Paragraph 7
slots.default: Yes. Bought through the right channel and registered with Apple Business Manager, a Mac can be delivered straight to the person who will use it. It enrols itself when they first switch it on, picks up your configuration and applications, and is ready to work without an engineer ever unboxing it. That is usually the single biggest time saving for a growing team.
